title.value: Usability of Virtual Reality Application Through the Lens of the User Community: A Case Study
title.justification: The title is directly stated at the beginning of the document and describes the focus of the paper on the usability of VR applications using community feedback and a case study method.
title.quote: Usability of Virtual Reality Application Through the Lens of the User Community: A Case Study

analysis.description: The paper studies the usability of virtual reality (VR) applications through user community feedback. It uses Firefox Reality as a case study to explore the types of usability issues and how existing usability heuristics, mainly Nielsen’s, can address these issues.

type.justification: The paper involves a case study analyzing real user feedback from GitHub and Oculus app store reviews, indicating an empirical approach.
type.quote: In this paper, we explore these RQs through a case study of Firefox Reality, an open source VR web browser developed by Mozilla.

name.justification: The paper focuses on usability, a key component of Human-Computer Interaction, as it relates to VR applications.
name.quote: The increasing availability and diversity of virtual reality (VR) applications highlighted the importance of their usability.

name.justification: The paper discusses Virtual Reality applications specifically, analyzing their usability through a case study with Firefox Reality.
name.quote: Function-oriented VR applications posed new challenges that are not well studied in the literature.

name.justification: The dataset of GitHub issues related to Firefox Reality was explicitly collected and analyzed in the study.
name.quote: We used the GitHub REST API to retrieve the GitHub issues and comments...
